title: Mirabel and the Choir
premise: Coral Ishikawa, a half-hidden cartographer for the Guild of Impossible Things, has spent his life keeping other people's secrets in ledgers no one was meant to read. When the border wards collapse and the stars go dark in a single night, Coral learns the ledgers record an old bargain: the realm's last dragon-fire sustains a binding that keeps a dead king's crown alive, and the thing wearing the crown has been trading the kingdom's light to keep its stolen shape. Guided by Mirabel, a choirgirl whose voice can steady unraveling magic, Coral must choose between the guild's code of silence and the truth that could save everyone. In the end, Coral unbinds the king at the cost of the guild itself, and Mirabel's choir becomes the new keeper of the flame, with Coral finally mapping a realm that includes himself.
about_author: Ulyana Sandoval is a former choir alto who spent a decade cataloguing rare maps in a private archive before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people who keep things — ledgers, secrets, fires — and what it costs to finally let go.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Impossibilities
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral catalogues a bottled thunderstorm and a debt of one forgotten name, revealing the Guild of Impossible Things and his role as its invisible record-keeper. The emotional beat is quiet pride in a hidden, orderly life — and the first hairline crack: a ledger entry he doesn't remember writing.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. The border wards fail at dusk; by midnight the sky is blank black. The guild masters seal the archive and forbid inquiry, but Coral recognizes the outage pattern from a forbidden page he once copied. The beat is dread curdling into defiance as Coral decides to look anyway.

chapters.title: A Girl Who Sings to Locked Doors
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. In the capital's orphan choir, Mirabel notices her voice makes the wardless doors hold shut, and the choirmaster watches her with hungry attention. She is summoned to sing for the crown. The beat is wary wonder — a gift that feels, for the first time, like a leash.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, with a court interlude. Coral travels to the capital to deliver guild tribute and glimpses King Aldous at the winter court: a man whose reflection lags a half-second behind his movements. The beat is cold horror — the ledger's oldest debt has a face, and it rules them.

chapters.title: What the Choir Remembers
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Singing at court, Mirabel feels the crown pull at her voice like a hook in her chest; afterward an old chorister tells her the choir once sang the binding that put the king on the throne. The beat is inheritance as burden — she is the last note of an old song.

chapters.title: The Guild's First Law
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral asks the guildmasters about the dragon-fire binding and is refused; worse, he finds pages of his own ledger razored out. His mentor, Vess, warns him that record-keepers who ask questions become records. The beat is loyalty strained to breaking — silence is the guild's first law.

chapters.title: Mapping the Dark
chapters.summary: Coral and Mirabel's POVs alternate. They meet by accident in the starless archive beneath the cathedral, where Mirabel's humming keeps the dark navigable and Coral's maps make it legible. The beat is cautious alliance: two keepers of different truths recognizing each other.

chapters.title: The Dragon's Last Ember
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Following a razored page's fragment, Coral reaches the Emberhold, where the last dragon, Serevaine, lies guttering — the living wick of the king's binding. She tells him the crown was never Aldous's choice. The beat is grief for something vast and dying, and a deadline: when she goes out, everything does.

chapters.title: A Debt of One Forgotten Name
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel discovers the razored ledger page hidden in the choirmaster's score: the binding requires a name freely given, and the name was Mirabel's grandmother's. The choirmaster has been feeding choristers to the crown for generations. The beat is betrayal — her sanctuary was a feeding pen.

chapters.title: The Guild Turns Its Face Away
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral presents his findings to the guild and is formally erased: his name struck from the rolls, his ledgers seized. Vess secretly returns one stolen book with a map to the crown's true vault. The beat is exile as liberation — losing belonging to gain a purpose.

chapters.title: The Road of Unmade Wards
chapters.summary: Coral and Mirabel's POVs. Fleeing the capital together, they cross countryside where unbound magic runs feral — rivers flowing uphill, roads forgetting their destinations. They learn to trust each other's crafts. The beat is growing partnership shading into something warmer, tested by fear.

chapters.title: The King in the Vault
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. In the crown's vault, Coral finds the real King Aldous: alive, diminished, woven into the binding as its anchor for thirty years. Aldous begs not to be freed — the thing wears his shape better than he ever did. The beat is devastating ambiguity about what rescue even means.

chapters.title: Songs the Crown Cannot Keep
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Mirabel learns the binding's weakness from the old chorister's dying confession: a name freely given can also be freely sung back. But singing it requires the full choir, and the choirmaster now guards the rehearsals like a jailer. The beat is resolve hardening into a plan.

chapters.title: Vess's Bargain
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Vess offers Coral a way back into the guild — erase the evidence, keep the ledgers closed — if he abandons the king. Coral refuses and watches the guild choose the crown's protection over the truth. The beat is the theme crystallized: loyalty to an institution versus loyalty to what's real.

chapters.title: The Ember Falls Low
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. Serevaine's flame gutters; the realm's remaining light dims to candle-strength, and panic spreads through the capital. The crown announces a great choir ceremony to 'restore the stars' — a mass feeding. The beat is the clock running out, hope and trap in the same announcement.

chapters.title: Infiltrating the Ceremony
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Using his erased status, Coral maps the cathedral's blind spots and smuggles Mirabel and two loyal choristers into the ceremony's ranks. Vess appears — and, in a quiet reversal, hands Coral the guild's master key. The beat is unexpected grace: the institution's conscience surviving inside one person.

chapters.title: The Choir of the Binding
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV. The ceremony begins; the crown draws on hundreds of voices, and Mirabel must sing along without being consumed, buying seconds by bending every note a hair flat. Coral works through the vault below. The beat is sustained terror — a duel fought entirely in music.

chapters.title: The Unbinding of King Aldous
chapters.summary: Coral's POV, climax part one. In the vault, Coral reads the binding aloud from the original ledger and offers the one thing that can replace a king's name: his own, freely given, written in the guild's master ink. Aldous is unbound; the crown, starving, turns on Coral. The beat is sacrifice offered without hesitation.

chapters.title: The Last Note
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, climax part two. As the crown seizes Coral's given name, Mirabel sings her grandmother's name back — freely, fully — and the choir catches the note and carries it, unmaking the binding from above while Coral's ink burns it from below. The crown collapses into ash; the stars flicker back, one by one. The beat is triumph earned at the edge of loss.

chapters.title: What the Fire Left
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Serevaine, freed from the binding, rises and departs eastward, leaving a single ember in Mirabel's keeping. The guild, its ledgers exposed, dissolves; Vess begins building something honest from its ruins. The beat is aftermath — the cost tallied, and found worth paying.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Own Name
chapters.summary: Coral's POV. Coral redraws the realm's maps with the wards restored and, for the first time, signs his own name to his work instead of the guild's seal. Aldous, a private man again, asks him to chart the dragon's road east. The beat is quiet joy: invisibility traded for authorship.

chapters.title: Mirabel and the Choir
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV, epilogue. The choir, rebuilt and free, sings the ember into a new warding-song that holds the borders and keeps the stars lit; Coral sits in the loft, sketching the sound. The beat is belonging finally earned — a realm mapped, a fire kept, a name sung home.
